extracted.intended_audience: researchers and faculty preparing grant proposals (NIH-focused, but generally applicable)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developing, writing, and submitting competitive research grant applications (particularly NIH-style applications), covering pre-writing, writing, and post-writing phases plus practical templates and pitfalls. Focus is on producing clear, fundable proposals aligned with agency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research the funding agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the agency's mission, review what kinds of grants it funds, and identify relevant program officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure mission alignment, study past funded grants to learn priorities, and identify key program officers to contact for fit/clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea development (conceptual framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the research idea through brainstorming, literature analysis, and a clear conceptual framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build an idea grounded in the literature, articulate hypotheses, and show how the conceptual framework leads to specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forming the team
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble co-investigators, consultants, and mentors appropriate to the project scope and aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include collaborators who supply necessary expertise and credibility; define roles and contributions clearly to strengthen feasibility and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims (foundation of the proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 2–4 hypothesis-driven aims that are independent but related, achievable within the funding period, and have clear endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep aims focused and testable; avoid diffuse or excessive numbers of aims; tie each aim to measurable outcomes and to the overall hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the problem matters, summarize what is known and unknown, and articulate how the proposed work fills gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the work in the context of the field and the funder's priorities; convince reviewers of importance and potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Present preliminary data that demonstrates feasibility, establishes credibility, and justifies the hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strong, relevant preliminary results prominently to show the project is viable and that the investigator/team can execute it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Design and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed methodology for each aim, including statistical approaches, alternative strategies, and a timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe procedures and analyses with enough detail to judge rigor and feasibility; include contingency plans and an explicit timeline linking tasks to aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Personnel (qualifications and commitments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document PI qualifications, roles of key personnel, and their time commitments to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the team has appropriate expertise and that committed effort (percent effort) is realistic and sufficient for proposed tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a realistic, detailed budget tied explicitly to specific aims and justified line by line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inflated or unsupported costs; show how each budget item enables the aims; choose modular vs. detailed budget formats per agency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Writing Phase (quality control & submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform internal review, mock review, final formatting, and develop a submission strategy before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for multiple rounds of revision and external critique; ensure compliance with formatting and submission system requirements to avoid administrative rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for the reviewer (Communication First)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize the reviewer's perspective: use plain language, define jargon, and make the application easy to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt clear, direct prose; label sections and figures for quick comprehension; highlight significance and feasibility early and often.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visual aids and clarity (figures, tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ figures and tables to clarify complex ideas and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-designed visuals can communicate methods, preliminary data, timelines, and conceptual models more efficiently than dense text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, don't just tell (evidence over assertion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims with preliminary data and citations to your and others' published work; use specific examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete evidence of feasibility and prior success strengthens reviewer confidence; avoid unsupported promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and address reviewer concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively identify likely criticisms and address weaknesses directly, offering alternative strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge limitations and propose contingency plans; showing you've thought through risks reduces reviewer doubts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time management for application development
rubrics_metrics.description: Start months in advance, allow time for multiple drafts and external feedback, and avoid last-minute submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule backwards from the deadline to allocate time for data preparation, team input, internal review, and administrative processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow agency-specific forms and formats (NIH PHS 398 / ASSIST / eRA Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere strictly to the agency's required application forms, formats, and electronic submission systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct form set (e.g., PHS 398 or ASSIST), select the appropriate budget format (modular vs detailed), and complete biographical sketches, other support, resources/environment, and cover letters per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare standard application components (biosketches, letters, timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sample-compliant biosketches, budget templates, timeline charts, literature cited, and letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recommended templates and examples to meet expectations for format and content; ensure letters of support document commitment and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid diffuse focus / too many aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the proposal narrowly focused—do not propose an excessive number of aims that dilute the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize aims that are tightly connected and feasibly testable within the funding period to present a coherent, fundable plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inadequate preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit proposals that lack sufficient preliminary evidence to support feasibility and hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary data are sparse, strengthen rationale with pilot studies, stronger methods, or phased aims; explicitly explain how feasibility will be established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unrealistic budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present budgets that are inflated, unsupported, or inconsistent with the scope of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie every cost to a specific aim or task and provide clear justifications; consult institutional officials for allowable costs and salary caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow reviewer instructions and agency guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to follow formatting, page limits, or other instructions risks administrative rejection or negative reviewer impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully check instructions for page limits, font sizes, required attachments, and conflicts-of-interest policies before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure good visual presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor formatting, unclear figures, or cluttered presentation can undermine the perceived quality of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clean layouts, readable fonts, and high-quality figures; make key points and data easy to find for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid last-minute submission errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting without allowing time for system issues, institutional approvals, or final checks can lead to missed deadlines or administrative errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan contingency time for electronic submission systems, institutional sign-offs, and corrections discovered at the last minute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates and sample documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage sample biosketches, budget examples, timeline charts, literature citation formats, and letter templates to construct the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates help ensure required elements are present and correctly formatted; adapt samples to your specific project rather than copying text verbatim.
